reason: Basi-dorsifixed anthers are still attached by the back. 'Near the base' only says where on the back, so FLOPO dorsifixed (attached by its back) holds. Basifixed (FLOPO_0991135) would be wrong, because the attachment is dorsal.

Hickey's leaf-architecture scheme, which PATO cites for actinodromous, lists flabellate venation as its own type: many equally fine veins fanning out from the base and forking towards the tip. So actinodromous makes a false claim. Fan-shaped (PATO_0002219) is a shape of the blade, not of the veins. No existing class fits.
The previous review mapped ventricose to FLOPO gibbous (C351). The negated rule follows that mapping, so 'not ventricose' = not gibbous.
Same as the accepted rule R1298 'drought tolerant': PATO tolerant to, with drought as the stimulus, on the whole plant. Here the stressor is part of the rule's word.

Pulpy maps to fleshy (R0084), so pulpy is narrower than fleshy. Negating the narrower word does not negate the broader one: a firm fleshy fruit is 'not pulpy' but is still fleshy. 'Not fleshy' would be a false statement.

Same as the accepted rules left-twining (R1211), voluble and twiner. The definition of FLOPO climbing includes twining. The twining direction is used inconsistently in floras and is left out on purpose.
FLOPO comose (FLOPO_0991171) already lists only seed|achene|cypsela|fruit as bearers. A tuft of hairs in leaf axils, on vein angles or at nodes is not comose.
A biglobular ovary or stigma has two rounded lobes, which is PATO bilobed. Dumbbell-shaped (PATO_0001876) would add a connecting neck that the text does not state.

Connate-perfoliate leaves are two opposite leaves fused at the base, so FLOPO connate is right. PATO perfoliate (PATO_0001983) describes the basal lobes of a single leaf joining around the stem, which is a different structure.

'Dust-like seeds' are extremely small, so the rule is decreased size, as with the accepted rule for 'minuscule' (R0878). On a surface, 'dust-like' may mean powdery (mealy), so the rule should apply only to seeds and spores.
The examples show a transcription join of 'a cuneate' ('tapering below into a cuneate base'), not a negation. The quality is PATO cuneate.

This follows the accepted cymose-corymbose and cymose-umbellate rules: the shape or arrangement is recorded, and 'cymose' (which has no value class) is left out. Flowers in clusters are FLOPO fascicled.
The statement is about the branches themselves ('branches not rebranching'), and on that bearer, unbranched is exactly right. The bearer slot keeps it off the whole plant.
FLOPO umbelliform is defined for inflorescences (PO_0009049). Umbellulate is a word for how flowers are arranged in the inflorescence, so the rule should apply only to inflorescence bearers.

Anther glands (for example in Mimosoideae) sit at the tip of the connective, so 'anthers without apical glands' means the anther has no glands. On other parts, 'apical' would leave other glands unaccounted for.
Same as the accepted rules 'broadest at the middle' (R1341) and 'widest in the middle' (R2071) = elliptic, which set it against ovate and obovate.
An inverted Y is the same shape facing the other way. Which way it faces is not a separate shape quality in PATO, and the examples are cross-sections.
On panicle branches and axes, 'profusely divided' means much branched. On leaves it means dissected (PATO_0104362), so the rule must not apply to leaf or blade bearers.

In plinerved leaves (for example Melastomataceae, Cinnamomum) the lateral primary veins leave the midrib above the base and often curve to the apex, which is acrodromous. Actinodromous claims more than the text says. FLOPO triplinerved (FLOPO_0991202) is too narrow, because there may be 5 veins. A broader 'plinerved' class over triplinerved would be the fix.
Same as the accepted 'tinged' colour rules (R0139, R0666, R1619, R1718). The colour is red brown, and 'tinged' becomes value_qualifier 'approximately' under pattern 01.
Same as the accepted rule 'tinged brown' = brown (R0991). The faintness becomes value_qualifier 'approximately' under pattern 01.
Follows the accepted 'tinged' colour rules. The colour is purplish red, and 'tinged' becomes the 'approximately' qualifier under pattern 01.

Resin coming from glands is still resinous. FLOPO resinous covers producing or bearing resin, and 'glandular' only says where the resin comes from. This matches how 'glandular-' compounds were handled before.

'Lateral bracts' are only some of the bracts, often paired bracteoles or prophylls. A part with a median bract but no lateral ones would wrongly get 'bract absent'. Bracteole (PO_0009043) does not fit the 'beside the receptacle' sense either.
Umbelliform with 'sub' as the approximate qualifier (pattern 01) is right, but the class is defined on inflorescences, so the rule should apply only to inflorescence bearers.

A plant that forms a low convex mound has a cushion habit, PATO pulvinate (as with the accepted rules 'mounded' and 'cushion-shaped'). On organs, pulvinate means a swollen pulvinus-like base, so the rule should apply only to growth-form bearers.
A multiheaded caudex divides into several crowns, so it is branched. In Asteraceae, 'multiheaded' on a plant or stem means several capitula, which is a count of capitula, not branching.
Follows the accepted 'tinged' colour rules: yellow with value_qualifier 'approximately' (pattern 01).
Silky is an exact synonym of sericeous. 'Short' is about hair length, a degree word, as in the accepted glandular-puberulous rule.
Hairs or scales with several rays are stellate (an exact synonym of PATO star shaped). On umbels or capitula, 'several-rayed' counts the rays or ray florets and is not a shape.
